summary: Enable conditional Confluence space cloning with ownership handshake and RBAC snapshot for ephemeral project spaces
description:
Background: Rapid experiment teams frequently request cloned Confluence spaces spun up from a canonical template. Current manual cloning loses a reliable snapshot of page restrictions and group membership, and onboarding owners is manual. This increases audit overhead and causes surprises when access needs to be reverted after a project ends.

Request: Implement an automated, conditional Confluence space cloning flow that: 1) performs a template-based clone of a source space; 2) captures and stores an RBAC snapshot (groups, page restrictions, explicit user grants) for the cloned space; 3) triggers an ownership handshake workflow (invites nominated owner(s) to accept ownership within a configurable TTL, default 72 hours); 4) returns the space to a quarantine/archive state if ownership is not accepted; 5) optionally creates matching Jira project skeleton and Slack channel with linked lifecycle hooks.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- A self-serve UI or slash-command triggers a clone with parameters (source template, owners list, ttl, create-jira, create-slack).
- RBAC snapshot is stored as an auditable artifact (read-only) and accessible to security/audit teams.
- Owners receive an email and Slack DM with an accept/reassign link; acceptance flips a 'live' flag and sets retention rules.
- If ownership not accepted within TTL, space is set to "archived-quarantine" and requestor + infra notified.
- Audit log entries created for clone and ownership events; Confluence page-level restrictions are preserved in the cloned space.
- Optional Jira project and Slack channel created when toggle enabled; each gets lifecycle hooks tied to the Confluence space state.

Why this matters: Reduces manual steps, prevents lingering access after short experiments, and provides an auditable RBAC snapshot for compliance reviews.

Proposed timeline: 3 sprints (discovery + design; automation prototype + RBAC export; owner handshake + lifecycle integration + rollout).

Contacts: Aisha Patel (Product, requester), Liam Chen (Platform eng, primary assignee), Priya Rao (Security reviewer)
acceptance_criteria: Self-serve clone action with parameters exposed in Console and via a slash-command
RBAC snapshot (groups, page restrictions, explicit grants) persisted and queryable by security/audit
Owner handshake invites sent (email + Slack) and accept/reassign recorded in audit log
TTL-based auto-archive/quarantine if no acceptance within configured window
Optional Jira and Slack resources created and linked; lifecycle sync to Confluence state
steps_to_validate: Trigger clone from Console using 'Clone with RBAC snapshot' option
Verify cloned space content matches template and page restrictions are present
Check audit artifact for RBAC snapshot containing groups and explicit grants
Confirm owner handshake message sent and acceptance flips space to live
Simulate TTL expiry and validate space moves to archived/quarantine state and notifications fire
If toggled, verify corresponding Jira skeleton and Slack channel exist and are linked
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Automated cloning could inadvertently grant broader access if RBAC snapshot applied incorrectly. Mitigation: Implement a dry-run mode that logs intended grants without applying them; require security approval for initial rollout to top-level spaces; limit self-serve to templates in a vetted namespace.
comments: Aisha Patel (2026-02-10): Filing because teams keep asking for quicker experiment spin-up with predictable teardown. Security wants an auditable snapshot of who had access when.
Liam Chen (2026-02-11): Adding initial acceptance criteria. Will investigate whether Confluence API supports clean export/import of page-level restrictions; if not, we will build a mapping layer.
Priya Rao (Security) (2026-02-12): Security: prefer RBAC snapshots stored in S3 with object versioning and limited KMS keys. Also require owner acceptance TTL not be shorter than 48h by default.
SRE (2026-02-14): Note: Slack channel creation requires workspace app scopes; will need a short security review of bot scopes and to coordinate with infra for app provisioning.
Liam Chen (2026-02-15): Marking pre-design complete. Next actions: spike Confluence restrictions export (ETA 2026-02-22) and prototype handshake emails/DMs. Linking related tickets.
investigation_notes: Confluence API: space export supports content and attachments; page restrictions available via REST endpoints per page (will need iterative crawl)
Potential privacy gap: explicit user grants on pages could include external collaborators—ensure export flags external identities
Slack provisioning: can create channels via admin API but workspace bot needs 'channels:write' and 'users:read' scopes; approval required
Jira skeleton: use existing project templates API; must ensure project key naming avoids collisions
notes_on_rollout: Initial rollout to 3 pilot teams (Model Evals, Growth Experiments, Integrations) gated by security sign-off. Monitor audit logs for 2 weeks; schedule rollback plan: disable self-serve and run manual cleanups.
slo_or_sla_notes: Not SLA critical; treat as product automation. Security review required prior to enabling for enterprise tenants.
follow_up_tasks: Spike: Confluence page restriction export (owner: Liam Chen)
Implement RBAC artifact storage (owner: Platform infra)
Build owner handshake UX and email templates (owner: Product)
